subject: Clarification on MSA publicity & reference rights
messages:
From: Julia Summers <julia.summers@brightpeak.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@brightpeak.com
Date: 2026-05-01T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on MSA publicity and reference rights

Hi Kimberly,

Our legal team reviewed the latest MSA + Order Form draft and flagged the publicity/reference section. A few concrete asks:

- The clause grants a broad license to use our logo and name for marketing without an explicit mutual approval hook. We need pre-approval for any logo use and a clear embargo window tied to product launch dates.
- The wording appears to make the license perpetual and irrevocable. That’s a hard stop for us.
- We need tighter limits on customer quotes and testimonials — any quote must be approved in writing and tied to an explicit sanitized quote template.
- Can you confirm whether reference calls are optional and whether we can request anonymization of metrics for public materials?

Attached: BrightPeak_MSA_questions.pdf (high level list from our counsel).

Would appreciate a short call this week to align.

Thanks,
Julia Summers
Head of Legal (BrightPeak)
+julia.summers@brightpeak.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Clarification on MSA publicity and reference rights (BrightPeak)

Team — forwarding BrightPeak’s questions. They’ve pushed back on the publicity/license language and want pre-approval + limits on quotes. Can Legal + CS propose firm language and ops constraints so Sales can respond.

My initial thinking: offer two practical options to reduce negotiation time:
1) Option A (balanced): Logo use allowed for customer announcements with prior written approval; embargo 14 days from mutual sign-off; quotes require written approval; no irrevocable license.
2) Option B (restrictive): Only customer name + anonymized quote allowed; logos disallowed; reference calls allowed but anonymized unless otherwise approved.

Naomi — can you draft the redline for both options? Marcus — what SLA should we offer for approving assets (3 BD? 5 BD?) and any operational caveats? Marissa — want to keep the deal momentum here, will tailor language to preferred option after Legal advises.

Attaching a stub redline I started: BP_MSA_v3_redline.docx (draft).

- Kim

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-03T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Clarification on MSA publicity and reference rights (BrightPeak)

Thanks Kim — read their PDF. High level legal notes (will put into formal redline):

- Remove any language creating an irrevocable or perpetual license to use BrightPeak’s marks. Replace with: "Customer grants Provider a limited, non-exclusive license to use Customer’s name, logo and a pre-approved short description of the relationship solely for Provider’s marketing and reference purposes, subject to Customer’s prior written approval for each distinct use."
- Define approval process: Customer shall respond to approval requests within 5 business days; silence is not approval. If Customer withholds approval, Provider will not use the asset.
- Embargo: propose 14 days standard, but allow Customer to propose a different date connected to product launch. Add: "No press release or public announcement shall be published by either party prior to mutual written approval."
- Quotes/testimonials: require written approval on final quote text and attribution; provide a sanitized quote template as Exhibit A.
- Reference calls: permitted with advance notice; Customer may request anonymization of any metrics used.

I removed the perpetual language and tightened definitions. I’m attaching the redline (BP_MSA_v3_redline.docx). Let me know if Sales wants a more permissive SLA (e.g., 3 BD) for high-priority launches — we can add an expedited review carveout in the SOW/Order Form.

— Naomi

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-04T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Clarification on MSA publicity and reference rights (BrightPeak)

Operational notes from CS/Marketing perspective:

- We can commit to a 3 business day SLA for approval if BrightPeak provides assets in the requested format (PNG/SVG + 2-line approved blurb) and tags a marketing contact. Otherwise standard 5 BD.
- We should offer a small marketing packet (logo pack + approved boilerplate) as part of the onboarding SOW to reduce back-and-forth. Note that some enterprise security teams want logos kept out of public asset buckets; we can scoping to a private partner assets folder.
- Reference calls: allow up to 2 reference calls in the first 12 months, with an option to extend. For public case studies, we must require written approval of the draft.

I’ll prepare a short ops paragraph to include in the Order Form attachment that commits to the 3BD expedited SLA when requested and provides the asset intake template.

— Marcus

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Julia Summers <julia.summers@brightpeak.com>, legal@brightpeak.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarification on MSA publicity and reference rights

Julia — thanks for the note and attached list. We want to keep things moving and have prepared two clean options for BrightPeak to choose from. Attached is a redlined MSA (BP_MSA_v3_redline.docx) that includes both options and an Order Form paragraph for asset intake/approval SLA. Summary below: 

Option A (Balanced; recommended for faster go-live)
- Logo use allowed for customer announcements and partner materials with prior written approval for each distinct use.
- Standard embargo: 14 days post mutual sign-off.
- Quotes/testimonials require written approval of final text.
- Reference calls permitted; Customer may request anonymization of metrics.
- Provider will not assert any perpetual or irrevocable license.
- Operational: 3 business day expedited approval SLA if Customer supplies properly formatted assets and a point of contact; otherwise 5 business days.

Option B (Conservative)
- No logo use allowed without an executed marketing addendum.
- Only Customer name and anonymized, non-attributable metrics or quotes allowed.
- Reference calls permitted but with anonymization as default.
- Same approval timings as above.

Please let us know which option BrightPeak prefers; Naomi has the legal redline ready and Marcus has the ops language for the Order Form. If you prefer, we can jump on a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments: BP_MSA_v3_redline.docx; publicity_guidelines_bp.pdf

From: Julia Summers <julia.summers@brightpeak.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: legal@brightpeak.com, press@brightpeak.com
Date: 2026-05-12T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Clarification on MSA publicity and reference rights

Thanks Kim and team — appreciate the clear options and the redline. BrightPeak prefers Option A but requests two adjustments before we sign: 

1) Embargo: we’d like 14 days as a minimum (we understand you recommended 14 as standard — we’ll keep that).
2) Add explicit language: "No press release or public announcement shall be published by either party prior to mutual written approval specifying the content and timing." (we want that spelled out in contract).

Also attaching our standard vendor marketing controls checklist (publicity_guidelines_bp.pdf). Please include the controls language about asset access and provide a brief note in the Order Form that assets will be staged in a restricted folder with limited access.

If you can send the final redline with these two tweaks, we’ll aim to close this week. 

— Julia
BrightPeak — Head of Legal
julia.summers@brightpeak.com
